analysis.title: Diamondback Energy Inc. (FANG): First Take: Beat on FCF Relative to GS and Consensus; Provides Color on Three Long-Term Permian Themes
key_insights: FANG reported 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of $3.75 bn vs GS estimate of $3.70 bn and FactSet consensus of $3.53 bn, a 1% beat vs GS and 6% vs consensus.
3Q26 FCF was $2.15 bn vs GS/consensus estimates of $2.03/$2.00 bn. Capital spending of $1,026 mn was in line with GS/consensus at $1,034/$1,012 mn.

FANG returned about $582 mn to shareholders in the quarter: about $331 mn of fixed quarterly dividends and about $251 mn of share repurchases. Net debt fell to $10.4 bn at 3Q26 end from $12.3 bn at 2Q26 end.

3Q26 adjusted EPS of $5.86 was 2% below the GS estimate of $5.97 and in line with consensus of $5.86. Total production of 1,034 Mboe/d was 3% above GS and 2% above consensus, with natural gas at 1,467 Mmcf/d vs GS 1,368.

4Q26 guidance: oil production of 518-528 Mbo/d vs GS/consensus 521/526 Mbo/d, total production of 1,025-1,045 Mboe/d vs GS/consensus 1,000/1,023 Mboe/d, and capital spending of $1.00-$1.05 bn vs GS/consensus $1.00/$1.01 bn.

Full-year 2026 guidance raised: oil production to about 524 Mbo/d from 522+ Mbo/d, total production to about 1,015 Mboe/d from 1,000+ Mboe/d, and capital spending to about $3.95-$4.00 bn from about $3.90 bn. Total cash costs were lowered to $7.80-$8.35/boe from $7.85-$8.65/boe prior, vs GS estimate of $8.05/boe.

The shareholder letter covered three Permian themes: improving recoveries (development design, completion design, enhanced oil recovery), gas production and monetization including easing pressure on gas realizations, and the role of AI and the power/infrastructure build-out in West Texas (fuel, land, water, deal execution).
Barnett position has grown 12% since February to 224k net acres, with drilling costs down more than 10% year-to-date. Management noted progress toward its cost target of $800 per lateral foot.

GS keeps a Buy rating and a $235 12-month price target against a $199.74 price, 17.7% upside. The target is based on an 11.5% FCF yield on 2027/2028 estimates at $80/$75 Brent and $3.50 Henry Hub, with an 85% weight on a fundamental value of about $231 and a 15% weight on an M&A value of about $259 (M&A rank 2).

GS's key questions for the 9 AM ET call: view on A&D and willingness to look outside the Permian, early Barnett learnings and 2027 activity, diversification of gas pricing exposure as Waha recovers, the relationship with VNOM given its underperformance, and 2027 service cost inflation.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 FCF beat GS and consensus, 2026 production guidance was raised and cash costs lowered. The target is based on an 11.5% FCF yield on 2027/2028 estimates.

earnings_insights: FANG 3Q26 reported adjusted EBITDA $3,752 mn vs GS estimate $3,700 mn and FactSet consensus estimate $3,528 mn (reported 11/2/26).
FANG 3Q26 reported FCF $2,148 mn vs GS estimate $2,026 mn and consensus estimate $2,004 mn. Operating cash flow was $3,174 mn vs GS $3,061 mn and consensus $3,017 mn.
FANG 3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $5.86 vs GS estimate $5.97 and consensus estimate $5.86. Cash flow per share was $11.34 vs GS $10.93 and consensus $10.99.

3Q26 realized prices: oil $85.89/bbl, natural gas $0.90/Mcf, NGL $20.02/bbl vs GS estimate $22.13/bbl. Total cash costs were $10.91/boe vs GS $11.26/boe, and all-in costs were $25.06/boe vs GS $25.26/boe.
GS estimates EPS of $19.32 for 12/26E, $22.32 for 12/27E and $21.27 for 12/28E. Quarterly EPS estimates are $5.85 for 9/26E, $6.80 for 12/26E and $6.13 for 3/27E, and 6/26 EPS was $6.65.
GS estimates FCF yield of 13.9% for 2026E, 14.1% for 2027E and 13.9% for 2028E, and EV/EBITDA of 4.7x, 4.5x and 4.3x.
